clue.text: Speed up set point serve

indicators.note: to serve something is to dish it up, here in a freshly arranged form

blocks.note: the eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A tennis player at set point is urged to hurry their serve.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom tells a driver or worker to go faster, so it is a spoken command to accelerate.

clue.text: Word to photographer gets husband's picture put up in church

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up means writing it from bottom to top
the turned-up pair is placed inside the church letters

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
to picture something is to see it in the mind
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A man's portrait is hung up in a church after a word with the photographer.
explanation.walkthrough: The picture word and the husband's letter are joined, turned upward, and set between the two letters for the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers ask subjects to say this word because pronouncing it forces a smile; the clue reverses roles playfully.

clue.text: Story line of Arsenic and Old Lace?

indicators.note: to lace is to weave or twist threads together, so the letters are interwoven anew

blocks.note: taken as written
O is a standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: It asks for the plot of the famous black comedy play Arsenic and Old Lace.
explanation.walkthrough: The title of the play and film looks like a single reference; it splits into the poison, an abbreviation, and a weaving instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is an outline of the plot of a play or film, which is a story line.

clue.text: Stumble with key change

blocks.note: F is a musical key
to change is to alter

explanation.surface: A musician trips up when the music shifts to a new key.
explanation.definitionFit: To falter is to lose strength or momentum and waver, just as one does when one stumbles.

clue.text: Grumpy teetotaller grabs last of lemonade before child's yet started

indicators.note: only the final letter of the drink is kept
whatever grabs something holds it inside its own grasp
only the first letter of the word, as it starts, is used

blocks.note: TT is the usual shorthand for a teetotaller
the final letter of the drink
CH is an abbreviation for child
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A teetotaller, irritable, snatches the lemonade before a child has even begun drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetchy means irritable and bad-tempered, a close synonym of grumpy.

clue.text: Quake with a bit of honest remorse

indicators.note: only a portion of the following phrase is taken, the letters running across both words

blocks.note: letters three to eight of the phrase

explanation.surface: Someone shakes while showing genuine regret.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a shaking movement, including a small earthquake, so it is a quake.

clue.text: Fool accepting credit note has trouble

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a sap is a gullible fool
CR is the accountancy abbreviation for credit
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: An idiot who takes a credit note ends up in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is an awkward predicament, an informal word for a spot of trouble.

clue.text: Very much always thus

blocks.note: ever means always, as in ever after
so means thus or in this way

explanation.surface: Someone gushes 'very much, always, thus' in an excited string of adverbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal British phrase, as in 'thanks ever so', is an intensifier meaning extremely or very much.

clue.text: Wind up in vintage car bound for cricket ground

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word sent up is read from bottom to top
the turned word is placed inside the car

blocks.note: something vintage is old
wind in the bodily sense, a crude slang word
a Ford is a make of car

explanation.surface: Someone cranks the starting handle of a vintage car heading to a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind up' looks like cranking an old engine; it is a rude word for flatulence turned upward, placed after 'vintage' and inside the car maker.
explanation.definitionFit: The Manchester venue is a Test match cricket ground, home of Lancashire, sharing its name with Manchester United's stadium.

clue.text: Church's help with tip-off to London police backfired

indicators.note: the tip, or first letter, of the word is taken off
something that backfires comes back the wrong way, so the joined letters run backwards

blocks.note: help without its first letter
the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: A church's call for help, tipped off to the London police, went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip-off' sounds like an informant's lead to the police; it means removing the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A temple is a building for worship, so it can stand for a church.

clue.text: Limb gets number inside after stretch

indicators.note: the number letter goes inside the limb word

blocks.note: a leg is a limb
N is the abbreviation for number
then means afterwards

explanation.surface: A limb takes an injection after a stretching exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: To lengthen is to make longer, which is what stretching does.

clue.text: Bird left eggs with partner

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
an O looks like an egg, so two eggs are two Os
in bridge, North is the partner of South

explanation.surface: A bird has abandoned its eggs to its mate.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players sit as North, South, East and West, with N and S partners, so a single compass letter can stand for 'partner'.
explanation.definitionFit: The loon is the North American name for the diver, a large water bird.

clue.text: Kirk's craft project?

blocks.note: first meaning: Captain Kirk's starship in Star Trek
second meaning: a bold undertaking or venture

explanation.surface: It asks whether Captain Kirk's vessel is a project of his own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kirk' could be the Scottish word for church; here it is the Star Trek captain.
explanation.definitionFit: The starship USS Enterprise is Kirk's ship, and an enterprise is also an ambitious venture or undertaking.

clue.text: Stay and stand some drinks

blocks.note: to stand something is to put up with it, to stick it
a round is a set of drinks bought for a group

explanation.surface: An invitation to stay at the pub and buy everyone a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick around is an informal idiom meaning to remain in a place, that is to stay.

clue.text: Pot's about to get gold lid, one cut out by Potter's mate

indicators.note: one is the letter I, which is cut out of the word it follows

blocks.note: C is circa, about
AU is the chemical symbol for gold
lid with its I removed
Ron Weasley is Harry Potter's best friend

explanation.surface: A pot is about to be given a golden lid made by a potter's friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' looks like a maker of pots, which fits the surface; it is Harry Potter, whose friend is Ron.
explanation.definitionFit: A cauldron is a large cooking pot, famously a witch's, which suits the Potter theme.

clue.text: Get into tripping in pleasant surroundings with drug that's legal

indicators.note: tripping suggests stumbling about, so the letters fall into a new order
surroundings tell us the pleasant word wraps round the reordered letters

blocks.note: nice means pleasant
taken as written

explanation.surface: An invitation to get high somewhere nice, using a drug that is lawful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tripping' sounds like taking a hallucinogen, which fits the drug surface; it only reorders the letters of 'into'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicotine, the addictive substance in tobacco, is a drug that can be bought lawfully.

clue.text: Sunbathe, say, in sexy bodice

indicators.note: say asks us to hear the word as spoken rather than as written

blocks.note: to sunbathe is to bask in the sun

explanation.surface: Someone suggests lying out in the sun wearing a sexy corset.
explanation.definitionFit: A basque is a close-fitting bodice, often worn as lingerie.

clue.text: Yay! Law punished ambush

indicators.note: something punished is knocked about and beaten into a different shape

blocks.note: the six letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone cheers as the law punishes an ambush.
explanation.definitionFit: To waylay someone is to lie in wait and stop them, which is what an ambush does.

clue.text: Bring back jelly roll for street kid

indicators.note: bringing something back returns it the other way round

blocks.note: agar is a jelly made from seaweed
a muffin is a kind of bread roll

explanation.surface: A request to restore jelly roll to the menu for a street child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jelly roll' looks like one cake, the Swiss roll; the two words split into separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragamuffin is a ragged, dirty child, the sort who roams the streets.

clue.text: Bush has accounts with international capital agencies

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its initial letter

blocks.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, doubled for the plural
I is the abbreviation for international
the initial letter of the word

explanation.surface: A political Bush is linked to accounts held with international agencies in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' looks like the US president; it is a plant. Writing the account abbreviation twice gives the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Acacia is a thorny shrub or tree, often called wattle, so it is a bush.

clue.text: Student's pursuing wife of major general

blocks.note: Norma Major is the wife of former British prime minister John Major
L is a learner, the plate on a student driver's car

explanation.surface: A student follows the wife of a major general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major general' looks like one military rank; split it, and Major is the former prime minister whose wife is Norma. 'Pursuing' places the student letter after her name.
explanation.definitionFit: General and normal both mean usual or typical, as in the general run of things.

clue.text: Pacific centre revolved around shellfish

indicators.note: only the middle of the word is spun round, its outer letters staying put

blocks.note: pacific means peaceful or calm

explanation.surface: Something at the centre of the Pacific Ocean whirls around a shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pacific' with a capital looks like the ocean, but it is the ordinary adjective for peaceful.
explanation.definitionFit: A clam is a bivalve mollusc, a kind of shellfish.

clue.text: Waste money on fancy sedan to carry queen with king

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or decorated, so the letters are dressed up in a new order
a car carries its passenger inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
QU is an abbreviation for queen
R is Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone wastes cash on a fancy saloon car to drive royalty about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sedan' is the American word for a saloon car, which suits the royal picture; here it is just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To squander something is to spend it wastefully, so it means to waste money on.

clue.text: Frighten betrayer, then let off

indicators.note: something off is wrong or out of order, so the letters are put in a different arrangement

blocks.note: a rat is someone who betrays their associates
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone scares an informer and then releases them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let off' reads as releasing someone; 'off' only reorders the three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To rattle someone is to unnerve or alarm them, a way to frighten.

clue.text: Diet or bust for newspaper man!

indicators.note: something bust is broken, and its pieces are rebuilt another way

blocks.note: the six letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A slogan urging a journalist to diet or else go broke.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor runs a newspaper, deciding what is printed, so is a newspaper man.

clue.text: Smart bird grasps cracked nut

indicators.note: something cracked is broken open, so its letters fall into a fresh order
what grasps something holds it within itself

blocks.note: a jay is a bird of the crow family
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clever bird holds a nut it has cracked open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' looks like clever, to suit the bird; it means stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaunty means lively and stylish, and smart can likewise mean neatly fashionable.
